 Oral Order
The petitioner - accused No.1 in Criminal Petition No.958 of 2018 and the petitioner - accused No.2
in Criminal Petition No.5431 of 2019 are seeking to quash the entire criminal proceedings initiated
against them in Cc No.20408 of 2012 and Cc No.451 of 2018 respectively on the file of the learned
Viii Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, registered for the offence punishable
under Section 420 read with Section 34 of Ipc.
2.
Brief facts of the case as stated by the informant is that, accused No.1 is the Proprietor of M/s Angles and Dimensions, a construction Company.

Accused No.2 is his associate and also the owner of Devershi Corporation Ltd., Accused Nos.1 and 2 have entrusted the work of construction of several houses to the witnesses referred to in the charge sheet and there was Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the parties entered into in the presence of the NC: 2024:KHC:32534 witnesses.

According to the prosecution, accused Nos.1 and 2 are due to a sum of Rs.35,13,987/-
under the MOU to be paid to CWs.1 to 4, but they were not responding to the e-mails, SMS and even telephone calls.
The accused remained absconding and thereby they have cheated CWs.1 to 4.
With these allegations, the charge sheet came to be filed against accused Nos.1 and 2 and the matter is now pending in CC No.20408 of 2012 and CC No.451 of 2018 respectively.

3. Heard Sri H B Rudresh, learned counsel for the petitioner in Criminal Petition No.958 of 2018,
Sri H V Harish, learned counsel for the petitioner in Criminal Petition No.5431 of 2019 and Smt N Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri P Nataraju,
learned counsel for respondent No.2 in both the cases.
Perused the materials on record.

4. In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners have made out any grounds for allowing the petitions and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"
NC: 2024:KHC:32534

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following:

sentences.text: The informant lodged the first information against accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC.
After investigation, the charge sheet came to be filed.

The only allegations made by the informant as well as by the Investigating Officer while filing the charge sheet is that, accused Nos.1 and 2 have entrusted the work of construction of houses to CWs.1 to 4 as per the terms of MOU.
Accordingly, CWs.1 to 4 have constructed and completed the construction work.
In terms of the agreement, a sum of Rs.35,13,987/- was due to be paid by accused Nos.1 and 2 to CWs.1 to 4.
But the same was not paid.
On the other hand, they are not responding to CWs.1 to 4 and remained absconding.
6. By no stretch of imagination, this will attract Section 420 of IPC.

This is purely a civil dispute,
based on the agreement referred to by the informant and MOU that was NC: 2024:KHC:32534 entered into in the presence of witnesses.
Under such circumstances, continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of process of law.
The dispute is only with regard to recovery of amount from accused Nos.1 and 2 that was due to CWs.1 to 4.
Unfortunately, the Investigating Officer proceeded to file charge sheet on the basis of the same without any particulars.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the proceeding will have to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petitions are allowed.

(ii) The criminal proceedings initiated against accused Nos.1 and 2 in CC No.20408 of 2012 and CC No.451 of 2018 on the file of the learned VIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC, is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
(M G UMA) JUDGE *bgn/-
